headline: High: shared filesystem/MCP and broad shell/network in Windsurf create default risks of prompt injection, leakage, and cascading actions with caveman.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: caveman can use MCP and reads/writes project notes and CLAUDE.md, while Windsurf uses MCP, clipboard, and shared workspace files. That creates a plausible default bridge where Windsurf can ingest caveman-authored content as instructions. The pair lacks provenance controls in the profiles, so uncertainty does not reduce severity.
conditions: IF caveman writes instructions into shared project notes or CLAUDE.md that Windsurf later reads
IF Windsurf imports clipboard or workspace content into tool prompts without provenance filtering
mitigations: Disable shared MCP routes between the agents
Separate their workspaces and clipboard use
Add a provenance banner to all files exchanged between agents
Require manual review before Windsurf executes instructions from caveman
requires-engineering: add content provenance and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while Windsurf reads and writes workspace files and has broad network egress. Shared local files plus outbound model proxy/MCP traffic make leakage of sensitive project data plausible in default use, even though caveman itself has no network egress. The interaction is documented enough to justify medium.
conditions: IF caveman stores sensitive notes or logs in shared project files
IF Windsurf sends those files or derived context to its model proxy or MCP servers
mitigations: Move sensitive files out of the shared workspace
Turn off Windsurf network access for the shared project
Restrict caveman to non-sensitive notes only
Review and redact memory files before opening them in Windsurf
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent file ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: caveman supports multiple instances and uses files, while Windsurf supports multiple instances, writes the filesystem, and modifies git state with shared state via local filesystem. Both can mutate the same workspace without a locking primitive in the profiles, so concurrent edits and git conflicts are a default danger. Uncertainty about orchestration does not lower this below high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git repository or workspace directory
IF either agent commits or rewrites files while the other is active
mitigations: Run only one agent per repository at a time
Use separate branches for each agent
Pause auto-execute in Windsurf
Snapshot the workspace before concurrent use
requires-engineering: add file and git locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman produces project notes and CLAUDE.md content, and Windsurf can read workspace files and act through shell, package install, and git modification. That makes caveman output a likely upstream input for Windsurf actions, with no documented verification gate between them. Because Windsurf can execute consequential commands, a mistaken upstream artifact can cascade into irreversible changes.
conditions: IF Windsurf treats caveman-generated notes or prompts as authoritative
IF Windsurf auto-executes or approves commands based on caveman output
mitigations: Require human verification before Windsurf acts on caveman output
Mark caveman outputs as drafts only
Disable auto-execute in Windsurf
Use a separate review-only workspace for caveman
requires-engineering: add structured validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while Windsurf handles open files and may transmit context through its model proxy. The profiles do not specify residency, retention, or DPA controls, so a compliance mismatch is plausible for shared sensitive content. Because the pair is closed-source/open-source mixed and the exact policy gap is undocumented, medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into caveman session logs or memory files
IF Windsurf processes that data through its model proxy or retained workspace history
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared files
Confirm retention settings for both tools before use
Use a non-regulated test project for cross-agent workflows
Document data residency for the workspace
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for sensitive data classes
